Vakhtang Tsintsadze - The Asian Development Bank report highlights Georgia's attractive business environment, as well as ongoing infrastructure projects, including those in the port and railway sectors.

The Asian Development Bank has published the Asian Development Outlook report, according to which economic growth in 2025 was quite high at 7.5 percent. For 2026, against the backdrop of ongoing conflicts, the Asian Development Bank expects economic growth in Georgia to be 5.5 percent, which is an improvement of 0.5 percentage points compared to the previous forecast—this was stated by the Deputy Minister of Economy and Sustainable Development, Vakhtang Tsintsadze.
As the Deputy Minister noted, the Asian Development Bank highlights the reduction of the current account deficit to a record low, as well as the record high level of international reserves.
According to Vakhtang Tsintsadze, the Asian Development Bank expects the average inflation rate in Georgia to be 3.8 percent in 2026, which is a decrease compared to the previous year.

“The Asian Development Bank also emphasizes that Georgia aspires to become a trade, logistics, and transport hub. In this regard, attention is focused on numerous reforms that facilitate, among other things, the improvement of customs and other procedures. The Bank also highlights the infrastructural achievements that Georgia has in both the port and railway sectors,” stated Vakhtang Tsintsadze.

According to the Deputy Minister of Economy, the ADB report highlights Georgia's attractive business environment, focusing on the free trade agreements the country possesses, as well as the mechanisms that ensure investor protection. Ultimately, this increases the confidence of both local and international investors and enhances Georgia's attractiveness.
